case_name: Commissioner, Municipal Corporation Hyderabad v P. Mary Manoranjani and Another
respondent:
P. Mary Manoranjani and Another
Supreme Court of India

11 January 2008
Appeal (Civil) 341 of 2008
The Judgment was delivered by: S. B. Sinha, J.
Leave granted.
1.  Respondent No.1 joined the services of Appellant-Corporation as Balwadi Teacher on an honorarium of Rs.100/- per month.

The Commissioner, Municipal Corporation of Hyderabad in his letter 2nd read above has stated that the Municipal Corporation of Hyderabad has been implementing the Urban Community Development Programme since 1967 that under this programme a number of Balwadi and Sewing Centres were opened in the slum areas for the benefit of the slum Woman and Children and a grant of R
facts: Respondent No.1 joined the services of Appellant-Corporation as Balwadi Teacher on an honorarium of Rs.100/- per month.

The Corporation requested the State of Andhra Pradesh to grant exemption in regard to requirements of sponsorship of the candidates by the Employment Exchange for appointment in the regular posts, pursuant where to G.O. Ms. No.27 M.A. (Q) dated 16th January, 1991 was issued,
issues: Whether the Government order exempting voluntary workers from the Employment Exchange procedure applies to this case
Whether the respondent has any legal right to continue in the said post
petitioner_arguments: The impugned orders of the High Court are ex facie illegal as in a case of this nature the aforesaid G.O. Ms. cannot be said to have any application whatsoever.
Any appointment made by a State within the meaning of Art. 12 of the Constitution of India must be subject to the constitutional scheme.
respondent_arguments: Keeping in view the tenor of the order passed by the learned Single Judge which has been affirmed by the Division Bench, as a mere direction for consideration of the case of the respondent in terms of the said G.O. Ms. has been made, no interference therewith by this Court is warranted.
court_reasoning: The G.O. granted only exemption from sponsorship of the names by the Employment Exchange.

Appellant did not and in fact could not ask for grant of any exemption from its obligation to comply with the requirements of Arts. 14 and 16 of the Constitution of India or other Statutory Rules operating in the field in this behalf.

Only when she came to learn of the fact that a complaint had been made against her, she requested either for her recruitment as a typist or grant her leave on medical ground, which ex-facie appears to be mala fide.
holding: The appeal is allowed. However, there shall be no order as to costs.
